scenario: AITA for wanting my girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks? She seems to forget that the way she lives isn't how most people live... | My girlfriend has a pretty sweet job. She doesn't have set hours; she just has to work 35 hours a week whenever is convenient for her and make it to her few meetings. She can work from the office or from home sometimes. She has a full benefits package despite being under what most people consider full time. A really nice retirement package too. And the company will pay everything for continued education. She does work she finds interesting (cutting edge robotics) and gets along well with her coworkers. She has a lot of PTO per year and her boss even lets the employees "earn up" more; if they work extra hours one week they can ask for the equivalent in PTO for later. Her team's managers buy them whatever they want for the office; they want a 500 dollar expresso maker, they get it. They want a type of fancy coffee, they get it. Nice furniture, done... They get paid well too; pretty middle of the road salary for robotics but she says the work life balance more than makes up for it. She'd rather have more time than be a top earner. And honestly a midrange robotics salary is still damn good. And anyway, For a while I thought "good for her" for having found something that she is happy with. But recently it's gotten frustrating because I think she forgets that this isn't how everyone lives. Like when we're out with my friends or just hanging out she'll talk about the nice stuff her managers bought for the office, about all the vacations she takes, about how she and her coworkers left the office in the middle of the day to see a movie then came back and just worked a little later. And yeah, it seems like she forgets that is no way a normal job. So last night we were at a party and she mentioned how she was going to tour a few new apartments Monday morning and afternoon, and one of the people at the party was like "don't you have work" and she said "yeah but I can set my own hours" And that just rubbed me the wrong way and I said that she needed to stop going on and on about her work perks, it was obnoxious and came off braggy. She was like "I was just explaining something" and I said it wasn't just this, it was everything. Most people don't live the life she lives." She said that I was coming off jealous and that it was a bad look. That she was where she was because she didn't settle for less; she studied and worked her ass off, and didn't let herself get too settled anywhere she was unfulfilled. And that instead of complaining, maybe I should ask myself what I'm feeling jealous of and what I need to do to get it. I told her she was missing the point; she'll always be around people who don't have what she does, and she could be a little more modest about it. She said I was the only one who seemed to have a problem with it, and stormed off... AITA for what I said?

Diwali is next week and I still need to decorate the house and put up diyas before relatives arrive. What would you prioritize first?

Diwali is just around the corner! Don't worry, I'm here to help you prioritize your tasks. Considering you have a lot to do, let's break it down into manageable chunks. Here's a suggested order of tasks to help you get started: **Immediate Priority (Today or Tomorrow)** 1. **Clean the house**: Give your home a thorough cleaning, especially the areas where you plan to decorate. This will help you get rid of any clutter and make the decorating process smoother. 2. **Plan your decorations**: Take some time to decide on the theme, colors, and design for your Diwali decorations. This will help you visualize what you need to buy or create. **Decorations (Next 2-3 days)** 1. **Lighting**: Focus on setting up the main lighting fixtures, such as fairy lights, candles, or string lights. This will help create a warm ambiance and set the tone for the rest of your decorations. 2. **Diyas**: As you mentioned, put up the diyas (earthen lamps) in strategic locations, such as the entrance, living room, and verandah. You can also make or buy diyas in advance to save time. 3. **Rangoli designs**: Create or buy rangoli designs to adorn your entrance, floors, or walls. This will add a beautiful and festive touch to your home. **Additional Decorations (Next 1-2 days)** 1. **Flowers and greenery**: Add some fresh flowers, garlands, or potted plants to enhance the festive atmosphere. 2. **Diwali-themed decorations**: Hang Diwali-themed banners, streamers, or balloons to add a pop of color and excitement. 3. **Final touches**: Add any finishing touches, such as decorative items, candles, or lanterns, to complete your Diwali decorations. **Last-Minute Tasks (Day before or Day of Diwali)** 1. **Final cleaning**: Give your home a quick once-over to ensure everything is tidy and ready for your relatives' arrival. 2. **Prepare traditional sweets and snacks**: Make or buy traditional Diwali sweets and snacks to serve to your guests. Remember, prioritize tasks based on your schedule and energy levels. Don't hesitate to ask for help if you need it, and enjoy the festive spirit of Diwali!

prediction.raw: I would say NTA (Not The Asshole) for what you said. Here's why: 1. **You're not being unreasonable**: You're not asking her to stop talking about her job entirely, but rather to be more considerate of others who might not have the same opportunities. It's not about being jealous, but about being aware of the privilege she has and being mindful of how her words might affect others. 2. **She's not being considerate of others**: Your girlfriend seems to be oblivious to the fact that her words might come across as bragging or insensitive to those who don't have the same advantages. She's not making an effort to be more considerate or understanding of others' perspectives. 3. **You're not asking her to change who she is**: You're not asking her to give up her job or her privileges, but rather to be more aware of how her words affect others. You're not trying to change her, but rather to encourage her to be more considerate and empathetic. 4. **She's deflecting and gaslighting**: By saying you're jealous and that you should ask yourself what you're feeling jealous of, she's deflecting the issue and making you feel guilty for pointing out her behavior. This is a classic gaslighting tactic, and it's not a healthy way to communicate. That being said, it's possible that you could have expressed your concerns in a more constructive way, such as: "Hey, I feel like you often talk about your work perks and it makes me feel a bit left out. I know you're happy with your job, but I feel like it's not always relatable to others. Could you try to be more considerate of how your words might affect others?" This approach would have allowed you to express your feelings without making your girlfriend feel defensive or attacked.
